messages:
Noah: FYI I'm submitting a docs PR that adds a small "mixed-workload" example to the Optimize toolkit. Users keep asking how batching + kv-prefetch behave when you have both low-latency streaming clients and high-throughput background workers hitting the same model. Draft PR: https://git.internal/redwood/docs/pulls/9124
Yara: Love this. Can we include a small CI test that runs a 30s mixed workload and asserts latency SLOs for streaming clients while measuring effective batch size for the background workers? That would be super helpful for regression catches.
Noah: Yes — planning a tiny example in examples/ci/mixed_workload.sh and a README paragraph describing expected metrics to watch.
Devon: Can you show how to collect the right metrics? People usually look at overall token rate and miss the streaming percentile. Suggest metrics to capture: redwood.stream_p95_latency, redwood.batch_effective_size, redwood.kv_prefetch_miss_rate, redwood.gpu_mem_alloc.
Noah: Will add them. Also including a small python microbenchmark that launches 2 streaming clients and 8 background workers. Snippet:
```python
# mixed_workload.py (pseudo)
from threading import Thread
from redwood import Client

def stream_worker():
    c = Client()
    for _ in range(50):
        c.stream_generate(model='rwd-3', input='short prompt')

def bg_worker():
    c = Client()
    for _ in range(200):
        c.generate(model='rwd-3', input='long prompt')

threads = [Thread(target=stream_worker) for _ in range(2)] + [Thread(target=bg_worker) for _ in range(8)]
for t in threads: t.start()
for t in threads: t.join()
```
Kei: Add a note that users should run it both with prefetch on and off and with two quant profiles (q4_0 and q8-balanced) to see differences. Also include expected outcome table: streaming p95 < 300ms when MaxBatchMs<=8 and prefetch enabled, effective batch_size > 8 for bg workers on q8-balanced, etc.
Yara: Also add a quick "how to interpret results" section: if stream p95 spikes while batch_effective_size increases, that's evidence background workload is stealing batches — recommend routing background workers to Dedicated or reducing their max_batch_size.
Devon: Small snippet to pull metrics from console for the 1m window post-run:
```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  "https://console.redwood.ai/api/metrics?names=stream_p95_latency,batch_effective_size,kv_prefetch_miss_rate&range=1m" | jq .
```
infra-bot: Note: internal infra doc link for metrics query examples moved. docs-bot will run link-checker on PR open.
docs-bot: @Noah scheduled snippet-lint + link-check on PR open. Will flag internal-only links.
Kei: One more practical tip: include a tiny troubleshooting checklist in the README for the example: 1) if stream p95 >300ms, check MaxBatchMs and set to 4 or 0 for streaming clients; 2) if batch_effective_size < desired, check q-profile memory footprint; 3) if kv_prefetch_miss_rate high, increase prefetch window or use per-route prefetch disable for streaming paths.
Noah: Good. I'll add exact config lines for SDKs (py/js) and show per-request override example. Py snippet:
```python
client = Client(batching={'enabled': True, 'max_batch_ms': 8})
resp = client.generate(model='rwd-3', input='hi', prefetch={'enabled': False})
```
Yara: Editorial: avoid saying "turn off batching" by itself; prefer showing the config key (max_batch_ms=0) and the per-route override.
Noah: Agreed. I'll update language. ETA: pushing PR in ~1h, pinging for review. :rocket:
